title: Epic Games MegaJam 2026
author: Kindly-Sail6260
selftext:
Now that the gamejam is over and everybody has submitted their games… it’s literally looks like a bunch of low effort slop 😭😭 man I was actually hyped for this year to see what kind of games people were gonna make and it’s lowkey full of garbage 🤧 

Now you might think four days isn’t enough for a game ham, but games have been made by a team or solo in that timeframe or less. It’s sad to see, but it looks like a lot of people just didn’t put as much effort as they should’ve in their games. 

Also the the was directors cut and people literally just fled to make the game, but didn’t listen what Dan Hutnik meant by that which was to make a game based on a mechanic that you had to cut out of a final past game or a mechanic you really wanted to try it but you didn’t have time to really invest in it. So most games are literal directors cut and some are straight copied IP’s 😭

Oh well, you can’t win em all. What do you guys think?

comments.author: CashFirm573
comments.body: I pulled out of the game jam due to fact it was directors cut, felt like such silly idea for a game jam, people would of just used old game designs what not to speed run game dev.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Well that was the point. They said you can freely do whatever you want essentially

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body: I poorly worded that, what I meant was people will just prompt "refactor this game of mine in unreal engine" wait several hours do some play tests then prob add few more features then submit.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Oh that makes sense. But that’s to say that they actually made the game before porting it over to UE.

replies.author: _KoingWolf_
replies.body: That was poorly put, to be fair

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: No game will be perfect for a game jam. Part of the charm is the jank, bug fixes and all. We’ll see how it goes. I just know they’re going to be sifting through a lot of games lol

comments.author: gryxitl
comments.body: I built 3 games in parallel with a swarm the first three days then cut down to one to polish extra hard and submit. That was really really intense haha.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Dang that sounds like a lot of work bro! 😭 three games in parallel is crazy but I guess that’s the whole point of AI. You don’t have to commit to anything until you know what you want lol

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
To call something a game which ai developed itself is not really fair to all the people who really try to learn gamedev. 
More of a showcase or technical demo. 

Developing three games in parallel is like developing no game but wasting a lot of tokens.

Developing a proper game in that timeframe is hard, especially if you have no experience. All the proper game Devs don't want to participate in an epic slop show which was clear from the beginning. Next fest was already bad and every other store is overrun by slop. Steam is the only shop which can manage because they don't ban it from there store. And then comes epic which prohibited ai games in their store anyways and tries to ride the ai fame train.

comments.author: SmokyBronco
comments.body: I was working on my submission and then went to the page to realize, I'm already an hour past due date/time. Dang, I got too busy over the last 4 days to keep up and for some reason had 11:59 tonight as the deadline in mind.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Bro noooo 😭😭 at least you can still finish it out and post it here. See how people feel about it.

comments.author: Bonelessgummybear
comments.body: I'm pretty happy with my game. It was stressful at though. First Shift is the name of my submission

comments.author: Daniele-Fantastico
comments.body: Not everything in the jam is junk. We developed a game that we definitely intend to keep working on. The result we achieved in just 4 days is, quite frankly, astonishing, even to us.

comments.author: Familiar_Relief7976
comments.body: It’s just because of AI I guess. I’ve participated in 2022 (and we’ve made it to 2nd place!) and it was only 500 submissions, out of which there were like 20-30 playable games. Now it’s almost 3000 games submitted and I believe now we still have decent 50-100 hidden somewhere inside, just difficult to get through all the slop. GL to juries, it would be a pain :(

comments.author: gjoconnor
comments.body:
When I first saw the theme reveal (on my phone with no sound cause I was with family), I thought it was dumb because of how specific it was. I couldn't see how people would differentiate their games enough with 'director's cut'. After trying to come up with something that fit, though, I thought 'eh, it's not terrible. There's some ways to be creative with it'.

And then I saw the email that gave the explanation and went right back to "this is the stupidest theme possible". The whole point of a theme is to level the playing field a bit and give guardrails that force more creativity. But now anyone can submit anything? I almost didn't join.... But went ahead with my original idea anyway.

It was my first time doing any game jam (because I'm not a real developer) so I'm happy that I at least followed through with a concept.

Serious question - how are they going to judge "A fresh, clever take on the theme" when the theme is whatever you want?

Also edit to say: Insane respect to game developers that do these game jams without AI and put out fun and novel experiences. Masters of the craft.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: I think the whole point was to see how far people can push unreal engine leveraging AI. It was definitely their version of PvP, but most people did the directors cut and I think if taken literally, would’ve been very difficult to get something unique. Most people literally made the exact same game lol hope to see your game out there!

replies.author: gjoconnor
replies.body:
Yeah, haha I thought most others would have heard the full explanation of the theme and NOT gone literally. Was hoping that mine would be different but..... with thousands of submissions of course a ton of them have the same name "Final Take" 😅

Learning experience.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Dang haha it’s all good though. What matters is that you finished it and now there’s a ton of other game jams that you can be a part of

comments.author: DVSoftware
comments.body: I burned half of my usage, and then I decided to abandon it. Theme was too vague. When I first saw the announcement, I was like, okay, I can work with this, but then when they said "make whatever you want"... nah...

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Ahaha I feel that. At that point you really have to think about what you want for the jam.

comments.author: AlphaPerzivol
comments.body: This comment makes me feel better cause my team’s game definitely has some jank to it. I had only made one terrible unity game before ChatGPT was even a thing. My partners had no experience at all. We all had fun and it was a good learning experience.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: The fun of creation is all that matters for game jams. Winning is the cherry on top. What’s your game called?

replies.author: AlphaPerzivol
replies.body: Our game is called From the Top. It’s about a bank heist similar to hitman and payday type games. Only reference to a director is the title and the final scene when you succeed. I’m also realizing we may have done better on the theme than originally thought. We found a jam game that had these unique mechanics of recording different characters’s movements and then replaying them together to achieve a goal. So we wanted to see how far we could push that idea. We credit them in our dev log. On top of that we just bounced around ideas for mechanics from different games to figure out what else to add. Other references that inspired us would be the movie Inception and the game by Ubisoft Watch Dogs.

replies.author: AlphaPerzivol
replies.body: Would love to hear anyone’s opinion on the game! It’s got some jank but the core I feel has promise for future iterations

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Sounds interesting can’t wait to try it!

comments.author: badandabiliday
comments.body:
Yes, I think the theme felt a bit vague, especially once the explanation came in. 

Our experience with game jams has been that some incorporation of the theme is generally looked favourably upon, even when the theme doesn't reference the content of the game, like in this case. That could be completely off the mark for this game jam for sure, but that was just based on prior experience. One of the judging criteria is 'use of the contest theme' so we had gone at it from both sides; this idea is one that had been kicking around for a long while, but we also thought it was an interesting creative challenge to work the theme into the gameplay itself with a hidden camera show.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Sounds good! Im just hoping to see what people will consider the too games of the jam. But with almost 3k submissions, it’ll be tough to find out.

replies.author: badandabiliday
replies.body: For sure, and the voting period says 4 months which is after the deadline they gave for the winners being announced. I hope that's an error, but with how long judging took last year it could take even longer.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Apparently last year was 500 submissions. Who knows how long it could take now. Could be crazy, but maybe they’ll use AI to play the games for them and use that to sift anything that doesn’t meen their minimum requirements.

replies.author: badandabiliday
replies.body:
I doubt it; they said all judges would be English-speaking, and the rules have specified that the panel will be made up of 'qualified judges' — additionally, based on the rubric, it might be difficult to have AI evaluate in the way Epic intends (for example, I believe a lot of the very literal approaches to the theme were ideas generated by AI). 

That's not to say they won't, of course, but I think it would be more likely that they would just bring more judges in.

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: If it’s like that then they’ll need a lot of judges to cover the amount of games on there. Some are definite blatant IP copies so they’ll be automatically disqualified. Saw an avatar one and I just knew they won’t get past the thumbnail. And some games don’t even have the actual game since it was past the deadline.

comments.author: ReflectionOdd9569
comments.body: My ai kept insisting that we needed to add director content. I was like ffs nooooo. I ended up doing 3 layers of director comedy tho, the rest of what it was trying to do was so cringe. I built something ive never seen, a cozy rave.. Xenofest earth.. it was meant to be more drawn out like the you are at rave aliens come the abduct everyone, you get free and save everyone but I didnt have time for all that.. so I just put it all into the best part which is the rave itself, aliens come and tske over with wit their tech. Its one of those things you just have to experience lol.. its definitely not infinite. ;p

replies.author: Kindly-Sail6260
replies.body: Sounds interesting!
